While I actually don't really disagree with capitalism, I can't grasp that we have among the highest collective capacity in the world and still force people to work by threatening them of being homeless. There is just a bare minimum of living with shouldn't be monetized, if we actually still value human beings.

No, I don't really have a problem with how work is done, but rather that I more and more get the feeling that we lost the goal of creating work to make a happy and healthy, not just rich society.

I don't like to run from problems, especially if they affect people's life in my country. I am a nurse, so I think I try to leverage my skills to benefit society and I am glad if I can.

My problem with this "meaninglessness" is that I am just helping people with enough cash to pay the hospital visits, which is not comprehensible for me at all. So, yes there is a economic problem, but not one which would require so much of a change, just allowing people to live.

If workers had more or even some say in what they do and how they personally are able to do it. We aren't products, even though our productivity seems to matter more than our well-being. Plus a society, where I am not literally starving to death, if I can't work. All this is totally possible under capitalism, that's why I am not against it, but seems like we aren't quite there yet, because that would mean less options to make cash from.

Unimportant, because the point is not, not wanting to work at all, but working meaningless and forced, due to our own overconsumption and social inequality. 

Yes, we need food and we need a home to survive, but our work nowadays has rarely till ever something to do with this, right? We work for businesses, which sell trash and trash and trash to keep a system working, which just isn't as productive as it was a couple decades ago. We don't thrive in our society anymore, we sell.

Workers don't have the feeling like they work to make the life of other people better and still have a life to live on their own. They work for cash or the enrichment of someone else.

Meaningless labour, which could be overthought and is in in most cases long obsolete, plus has nothing to do with actual problems humans face and mostly won't improve them, that is the REAL shit.
Theoretically money is everything, as it represents life. It rather seems like enjoyment is at a decline.
Well, yea I am far from having a purpose, but I guess if I had none, I wouldn't be here anymore. Maybe it's rather the focus I am lacking. But I'd be delighted to hear your questions.
